key_insight: AlgoRAG shows that a domain-tuned RAG system can reliably teach theoretical computer science by combining authoritative course materials with notation-aware retrieval and pedagogical ranking.
engineering_relevance: This work suggests that educational AI for proofs and algorithm analysis can be improved by retrieval design tailored to math notation, curriculum structure, and explanation quality rather than generic text similarity.
method: Curated TCS knowledge base from textbooks, slides, practice problems, proof templates, and worksheets
Domain-specific retrieval with mathematical entity recognition and notation-aware matching
Pedagogical re-ranking to favor explanations that are clearer and more instructional
evidence_signal: Evaluated on 179 exam-style questions across core TCS topics, AlgoRAG achieved 100% success with mean response time of 38.0 seconds and strong pedagogical quality despite low n-gram overlap scores.
watch_item: BLEU-4 is zero, highlighting that standard automatic text metrics can miss mathematically correct solutions when equivalent reasoning is expressed with different notation.
paper_title: AlgoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Theoretical Computer Science Education -- A Comprehensive Evaluation Framework for Algorithm Analysis and Complexity Theory
